This tutorial covers the core of theoretical physics. It goes from classical mechanics, electromagnetism and statistical mechanics
to quantum mechanics, field theory, gauge theories and renormalisation, and then to special and general relativity, supersymmetry
and supergravity.

Each chapter sets out definitions and results, works through examples, and gives exercises to try. It uses the mathematics from
[Fundamentals of Mathematics for Physicists](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/index.qmd), and links back to it where a
result is needed. It also leads into [Kaluza-Klein Theories](../kaluza-klein-theories/index.qmd).

## Chapters

- [Classical mechanics](part-ii-01-classical-mechanics.qmd)
- [Classical electromagnetism](part-ii-01b-electromagnetism.qmd)
- [Thermodynamics and statistical mechanics](part-ii-02-thermodynamics-statistical-mechanics.qmd)
- [Quantum mechanics](part-ii-03-quantum-mechanics.qmd)
- [Classical field theory](part-ii-04-classical-field-theory.qmd)
- [The Dirac equation](part-ii-05-dirac-equation.qmd)
- [Quantum field theory](part-ii-07-quantum-field-theory.qmd)
- [Gauge theories](part-ii-06-gauge-theories.qmd)
- [Renormalisation](part-ii-08-renormalisation.qmd)
- [Special relativity](part-ii-08b-special-relativity.qmd)
- [General relativity](part-ii-09-general-relativity.qmd)
- [Supersymmetry and supergravity](part-ii-10-supersymmetry-supergravity.qmd)

This tutorial has its own [glossary](glossary.qmd) and [verification registry](registry.qmd). Works cited are listed at the end of each chapter.
